name: Mirissa
line: A bay for whale watching from November to April, and slow evenings after.

image.alt: Palms on a red headland above the sea at Mirissa

summary: A small bay on the south coast, and the best place on the island to go looking for blue whales.

intro.heading: Whales, then a slow evening.
paragraphs: Mirissa is a curve of sand with a fishing harbour at one end. From November to April, blue whales and sperm whales pass close to the south coast, and the boats go out from here at dawn.
The beach itself has filled up with bars over the years. We book stays on the quieter headlands either side, so the whale morning is followed by a long lunch and not much else.

mapCaption: On the south coast, east of Galle. The other dots are the places we pair it with.

doing.lede: Mirissa is a morning at sea and an afternoon off. These are the things we build the days around.

items.title: A whale watching morning
items.body: Out at six, back by lunch. We use operators who keep their distance from the whales, and we only go in season.

items.title: Coconut Tree Hill
items.body: A red headland crowded with palms, a short walk from the beach. Best at the end of the day.

items.title: A first surf lesson
items.body: The small waves at the western end of the bay suit beginners. Boards and a patient instructor are easy to find.

items.title: Fish on the beach at night
items.body: The day’s catch laid out on ice along the sand. Pick one, and it is grilled while you wait.

gallery.alt: A headland and bay on the south coast from the air
A walker among the palms on a red headland above the sea

season: Mirissa follows the south coast: calm and dry from December to April, rough and wet while the south west monsoon blows from May to September. The whales are here from November to April.
ctaBody: Tell us your dates and we will fit it in, with the whale morning in the right month.
